title: Tiramisu
desc: An egg-free version with coffee-soaked biscuits and mascarpone cream.
steps: Stir mascarpone and icing sugar together until smooth. Whip cream separately to soft peaks and fold into the mascarpone.
Pour cooled coffee into a shallow bowl. Dip biscuits briefly on both sides, without soaking until soggy.
Layer half the dipped biscuits and half the cream mixture in a 20 × 25 cm dish for the base batch. Repeat the layers.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours. Dust with cocoa just before serving; keep leftovers refrigerated and use within 2 days.

title: Crème Brûlée
desc: Vanilla custard under a crisp caramel crust.
steps: Preheat to 140°C conventional. Set shallow heatproof ramekins in a roasting tray. Warm cream and vanilla until steaming, without boiling.
Whisk yolks and sugar gently, then slowly pour in warm cream while stirring. Strain and divide between ramekins, about 100 ml per portion.
Pour hot water into the roasting tray halfway up the ramekins. Bake for 35–45 minutes until the edges are set and centres gently tremble, without liquid ripples.
Remove from the water, cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Divide topping sugar evenly over the chilled custards. Caramelise with a kitchen torch, keeping it moving, and let the crust harden for 2 minutes before serving.

title: Vanilla Panna Cotta
desc: Soft vanilla cream set in individual glasses.
steps: Pour cold milk into a bowl and sprinkle gelatine evenly over it. Leave for 10 minutes to hydrate.
Warm cream and sugar in a saucepan, stirring until sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat before boiling.
Stir in the soaked gelatine and milk until fully dissolved, then add vanilla. Strain into a jug.
Divide between serving glasses, cool briefly, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours until softly set. Serve in the glasses.

title: Chocolate Mousse
desc: An egg-free dark chocolate mousse with whipped cream.
steps: Put chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Heat the cream for sauce until steaming and pour it over the chocolate.
Wait for 2 minutes, then stir until smooth. Cool to lukewarm, about 35°C, while keeping it fluid.
Whip the cream for filling to soft peaks. Fold a little into the chocolate to loosen it, then fold in the rest gently.
Spoon into glasses and refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Serve chilled and use within 2 days.

title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
desc: A warm date sponge with buttery toffee sauce.
ingredients: Eggs, beaten and weighed without shells
steps: Preheat to 160°C fan and line a 20 cm square tin for the base batch. Pour boiling water over dates, stir in bicarbonate and leave for 10 minutes; mash lightly.
Beat softened butter with brown sugar until creamy. Beat in eggs gradually, then fold in flour and baking powder.
Fold in the dates and all their soaking liquid. Pour into the tin and bake for 30–40 minutes until springy and a skewer comes out clean.
Heat the sauce sugar, sauce butter and cream together. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until smooth and slightly thickened.
Rest the pudding for 10 minutes, then cut into portions and serve warm with the sauce.

title: Apple Crumble
desc: Baked apples under a crisp oat crumble.
steps: Preheat to 180°C fan. Toss apples with brown sugar, lemon juice and cinnamon in a 20 × 25 cm baking dish for the base batch.
Rub flour and cold diced butter together until crumbly.
Stir sugar and oats into the crumbs and scatter loosely over the apples, without pressing down.
Bake for 35–45 minutes until golden and the fruit bubbles at the edges. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Bread Pudding
desc: Bread baked in vanilla custard with sultanas.
ingredients: Eggs, beaten and weighed without shells
steps: Preheat to 160°C fan. Butter a deep 20 × 25 cm dish for the base batch and fill with bread and sultanas.
Whisk eggs, sugar, milk, cream, vanilla and cinnamon until blended.
Pour over the bread and press lightly to soak. Leave for 20 minutes.
Bake for 40–50 minutes until golden and the centre is set with no liquid custard. Rest for 10 minutes and serve warm.

title: Lemon Posset
desc: A silky lemon cream set without eggs or gelatine.
steps: Put cream and sugar in a saucepan with plenty of headroom.
Bring to a gentle boil, stirring to dissolve the sugar, and simmer for 3 minutes. Watch closely to prevent boiling over.
Remove from heat and stir in lemon juice. Leave for 10 minutes, then strain into small serving glasses.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set. Serve chilled.

title: Profiteroles
desc: Cream-filled choux shells with warm chocolate sauce.
steps: Use the prepared baked choux shells, completely cooled. Split each shell horizontally.
Whip filling cream with icing sugar to soft peaks. Spoon or pipe into the lower halves and replace the tops.
Put chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Heat sauce cream until steaming, pour over chocolate and stir until smooth.
Let the sauce cool until just warm, then drizzle over the filled shells and serve immediately. Keep filled shells refrigerated if waiting briefly.

title: Chocolate Lava Cake
desc: Individual chocolate cakes with a soft centre.
steps: Preheat to 180°C fan. Butter individual 150 ml heatproof moulds and dust with cocoa, tapping out excess.
Melt chocolate and butter gently together and cool until lukewarm.
Whisk pasteurised eggs and sugar until thick. Fold in the chocolate mixture, then sift in flour and fold just until combined.
Divide evenly between moulds and bake for 10–13 minutes until the edges are set but centres remain soft. Rest for 1 minute, loosen the edges and turn out carefully; serve immediately.

title: Vanilla Ice Cream
desc: A churned vanilla ice cream with a cooked custard base.
steps: If required, freeze the ice-cream machine bowl according to its instructions. Warm milk, cream and vanilla until steaming.
Whisk yolks and sugar together. Slowly pour in the warm dairy while whisking, then return to the saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring continuously, until the custard coats a spoon and reaches 82°C. Do not boil; strain into a clean bowl.
Cool the bowl in an ice-water bath, stirring, then cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until thoroughly cold.
Churn according to the machine instructions, then transfer to a freezer container and freeze for at least 3 hours until scoopable.
